title: Sliding canary with composite SLO gates, shadow validation and automated rollback choreography
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce sliding-canary rollout strategy with composite SLO gates (latency/error/quality), shadow validation hooks and automated rollback choreography. Backwards compatible with existing canary config; new strategy opt-in via rollout.strategy.type="sliding-canary".
description:
Motivation: Customers running mixed-quality-sensitive workloads asked for a rollout mode that can: (1) evaluate live traffic quality (semantic/regression metrics) alongside traditional SLOs (p50/p95 latency, error rate), (2) apply a gradual sliding window increase in traffic rather than fixed steps, and (3) wire automated rollback choreography when any composite gate trips while preserving an audit trail and optional shadow replay for offline bisect.

This PR implements a new rollout strategy named 'sliding-canary' in the rollout controller and adds telemetry-driven composite gates that aggregate signals across latency, error rate, and configured application-level quality checks (e.g., eval-set regression score). The strategy supports: sliding traffic ramps (percent per minute), safety holdpoints with manual approval, shadow capture for failing slices, and coordinated rollback with tokenized rollback-playbook events for operator playbooks.

Key user-visible changes:
- New rollout.strategy.type = "sliding-canary" with fields: start_percent, max_percent, slide_rate_per_min, hold_points[], composite_gates[]. Each composite_gate can reference latency/error thresholds and quality metric expressions.
- New API endpoints: POST /rollouts/:id/snapshot and POST /rollouts/:id/force-hold for operator intervention.
- Shadow capture toggle at rollout level to mirror traffic for offline replay and automated bisect.
- Automated rollback choreography: when a composite gate trips, controller emits a rollback token and sends a structured event to the playbook queue; optional dry-run replays can be configured.

Design summary:
- Controller: implements time-windowed sliding window sampler (defaults to 60s windows) collecting per-route aggregated signals. Composite gates evaluate historical windows with configurable decay to prevent single-spike noise.
- Telemetry: added new rollup metrics (rollout.window_latency_p95, rollout.window_error_rate, rollout.window_quality_regression) and tags for rollout_id, cohort. These feed into the composite gate evaluator and the console dashboards.
- Shadowing: lightweight capture stores request metadata + model-output fingerprint in compressed sstable and emits a pointer to object storage. Replay harness reuses existing replay infra but tags traces with original rollout cohort for bisect.
- Safety: built-in backoff policy on rollback that respects operator holdpoints and supports an autorecover mode if upstream transient issue resolves (configurable cooldown).

Migration/backcompat: existing rollout configs are unchanged; sliding-canary is opt-in. Controllers running older versions ignore sliding-canary rollouts and return a validation error prompting users to upgrade. Migration doc included.

Tests & CI: unit tests for gate evaluation, e2e integration tests for sliding ramp behavior and rollback choreography, and a small load test simulating mixed-quality degradation.

Commits (summary):
- add: rollout strategy implementation (controller + reconciler + leader-election safety)
- add: composite gate evaluator and config schema + validation
- add: telemetry metrics and console dashboard panels
- add: shadow capture writer and replay tagging
- add: API endpoints for snapshot/force-hold
- fix: reconciliation race on concurrent rollout updates
- chore: docs + migration guide + rollout strategy examples

Changed files (high level):
- controller/rollouts/strategy_sliding_canary.go (new)
- controller/rollouts/gate_evaluator.go (new)
- api/rollouts/routes.go (api additions)
- telemetry/metrics_rollouts.prom (metrics defs)
- observability/dashboards/sliding_canary.json (dashboard)
- replay/harness/capture_writer.go (shadow capture)
- docs/runbooks/sliding-canary.md (user guide + migration)
- tests/integration/sliding_canary_e2e.test (test harness)
- ci/workflows/rollout-integration.yml (updated to include new e2e)

Short code snippet (controller):
- sliding window aggregator uses exponential-decay on per-window aggregates to reduce sensitivity to one-off spikes.

Testing notes: e2e run against local dev cluster simulates a regression in 'semantic-fidelity' quality metric between 0.86 -> 0.72 which correctly trips the composite gate after three sliding windows and triggers the rollback token and shadow capture pointer. The replay harness successfully replays captured traffic slice and reproduces the regression in offline evals.

Security & perf considerations: shadow capture stores only fingerprints and minimal context by default (PII scrubbed); customers can opt into full request store under explicit consent. The sliding window evaluator is bounded-memory and runs on controller leader only. Benchmarks show <5% controller CPU increase at 1000 concurrent rollouts.

Rollback playbook example: 
1) Gate trips -> controller emits rollback token with metadata
2) Orchestrator pauses traffic ramp and issues rollback command to serving plane
3) Shadow capture pointer is sent to replay service for bisect
4) Operator can either approve autorecover or approve manual revert

Docs & examples: docs/runbooks/sliding-canary.md shows example YAML, A/B experiment mapping, and guidance for tuning composite gates (weighting latency vs quality).

Why this is different from existing canary strategies: rather than incrementing in fixed steps, sliding-canary performs continuous ramping evaluated in sliding windows and uses a composite evaluation function that can incorporate domain-specific quality signals (not just latency/error), enabling safer ramping for quality-sensitive models such as summarization or reranking.

Related: ENG-3245 (composite SLOs), ENG-3310 (shadow replay improvements).
review_conversation: Daniel Kim (reviewer): Left a couple of inline comments on gate evaluator edge cases — specifically around window decay math and handling empty windows. Requested adding a unit test for empty-slice behavior.
Asha Patel (author): Addressed. Added unit test and clarified decay constant comments. Also added a guard that treats empty windows as 'no signal' instead of 0 to avoid false positives.

Priya Nair (reviewer): Question about operator UX for force-hold — requested clearer error messages when attempting to hold a rollout that already completed. Also asked for more explicit docs on PII handling for shadow capture.
Asha Patel (author): Updated API error codes and docs. Shadow capture now defaults to fingerprint-only; docs include opt-in instructions and required consent flow.
Owen Martinez (approver): Verified e2e runs in staging and approved. Noted one follow-up: consider adding a 'snapshot diff' comparator to console in a separate PR.
CI bot: All checks passed (unit, integration, lint). Integration had 1 flaky test which was re-run and passed.
